purpose: Worksheet of candidate datasets with the licence evidence verified so far, in the exact shape the dataset API accepts. Nothing here is approved and nothing was downloaded. Load it into a workspace with `python -m app.tools.dataset_worksheet` (dry run by default), which uses the same service code as the API; do not paste candidate URLs into the app expecting it to fetch them (it never fetches).

how_evidence_was_verified.read_in_full_text: The text was extracted locally from the document (pdftotext) and read; quotes are exact.
how_evidence_was_verified.page_reader_tool_quote: A page-reading tool summarised the page and returned fragments inside quotation marks; only those fragments are quoted here, and they were not compared against the raw HTML. Treat as official-source evidence that a person should re-confirm before relying on it for approval.
how_evidence_was_verified.api_json_field: A field of the host's machine-readable record (for example the Zenodo API), reproduced as returned.

owner_decisions: PlantDoc remains excluded (2026-10-18); its authors are not to be contacted and it is not to be approved unless the owner explicitly authorises that later.

entries.outcome: EXCLUDED by owner decision; also blocked by image origin
verified: The official repository README states 'Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International' for the dataset.
The paper (arXiv 1911.10317) says the images were scraped from Google Images and Ecosia and does not discuss copyright or licensing.
unresolved: The authors' right to license scraped third-party images (a hosting repository's licence is not proof of that)
Commercial use and redistribution are not stated on the pages read

catalog.name: PlantDoc
catalog.intended_use: Not to be used: excluded by owner decision

entries.outcome: EXCLUDED by policy: the creators' own terms are CC BY-SA 3.0 with a clause extending it to trained algorithms
entries.recommended_action: An owner or admin should reject this dataset in the catalog.
verified: The dataset paper by the creators (Hughes and Salathe, arXiv 1511.08060, read in full text) states the licence as CC BY-SA 3.0 with the clarification that algorithms trained on the data fall under the same licence.

The same paper says all images were taken at experimental research stations associated with Land Grant Universities in the USA, with a camera, against paper backgrounds (lab-like conditions): the images are the creators' own.
PlantVillage's own terms of service say its content is licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 unless marked otherwise (tool-reported quote).
The widely used GitHub mirror (spMohanty/PlantVillage-Dataset) states no licence and is not the creators' site, so it is not evidence of any licence.
unresolved: Whether PlantVillage has since re-licensed the data: no such statement was found on the official pages read, and the terms page offers no downloadable dataset
Whether CC0 claims on derived copies have any basis (none found at the source)

catalog.name: PlantVillage
catalog.attribution_text: Hughes, D. P. and Salathe, M. (2015). An open access repository of images on plant health to enable the development of mobile disease diagnostics. arXiv:1511.08060
catalog.intended_use: Not to be used: share-alike licence is excluded by policy; lab imagery also overstates field performance

evidence.excerpt: openly accessible and released under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported (CC BY-SA 3.0), with the clarification that algorithms trained on the data fall under the same license.
"All Content (other than computer software) made available by PlantVillage" ... "licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 License, unless marked otherwise."

entries.outcome: BLOCKED: licence verified; image origin (who photographed, with what permission) unresolved
verified: Mendeley Data (the host) shows the licence 'CC BY 4.0' for this dataset (DOI 10.17632/3832tx2cb2.1), authors L G Divyanth, Peeyush Soni, Rajendra Machavaram, IIT Kharagpur, published 30 November 2021 (tool-reported).
The record says the images were 'collected manually from different commercial agricultural fields in western Tamil Nadu, India' using a handheld camera.
Creative Commons states that CC BY 4.0 allows copying, redistribution and adaptation 'for any purpose, even commercially', with credit required.

The Mendeley footer says all rights are reserved including text and data mining and AI training, and, on another page of the same site, 'For all open access content, the Creative Commons licensing terms apply.' The two sentences are not reconciled on the pages read; the dataset-level CC BY 4.0 label governs open-access datasets according to that second sentence.
unresolved: Who took the photographs and whether the owners of the commercial fields permitted publication (the page does not name the photographer)
No associated paper was found that would document collection and labelling; label provenance and quality are undocumented
The site-wide text-and-data-mining reservation sits beside the CC BY label: ask Mendeley or the authors how the two interact before training a model

catalog.attribution_text: L G Divyanth, Peeyush Soni, Rajendra Machavaram. Cassava Leaf Disease Dataset. Mendeley Data, V1, 2021. DOI 10.17632/3832tx2cb2.1. Licensed under CC BY 4.0.
catalog.intended_use: Single-crop (cassava) leaf-condition classification baseline, only once image origin is resolved

evidence.excerpt: "copy and redistribute the material in any medium or format for any purpose, even commercially." "You must give appropriate credit, provide a link to the license, and indicate if changes were made."

entries.outcome: BLOCKED: dataset-level CC BY 4.0 verified; licences of the individual contributed images not established; species identification, not disease
verified: The Zenodo record's machine-readable metadata gives the licence {"id": "cc-by-4.0"}; access 'open'; creators Garcin, Joly, Bonnet, Affouard, Lombardo, Chouet, Servajean, Lorieul, Salmon; version 1.1; DOI 10.5281/zenodo.5645731.
The record says the dataset is 'built from the database of Pl@ntNet citizen observatory' and asks users to cite the NeurIPS 2021 paper.

The code repository is BSD-2-Clause (code only) and says the metadata file maps each image to information including 'author, license' (per-image licences exist in the data but their values were not read).
Neither the Zenodo record nor the Pl@ntNet open-data page states commercial-use terms, redistribution terms beyond the licence, or per-image licences.
unresolved: The licence of each contributed image (the metadata file would answer this; it is inside the dataset download, which is not permitted before approval)
Whether the creators could license contributors' images under CC BY 4.0 for the whole dataset
Relevance: species identification, not plant health

catalog.name: PlantNet-300K
catalog.attribution_text: Garcin et al. Pl@ntNet-300K: a plant image dataset with high label ambiguity and a long-tailed distribution. NeurIPS 2021 Datasets and Benchmarks. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.5645731.
catalog.intended_use: Species identification only, if per-image licences are established

entries.outcome: BLOCKED: dataset-level CC BY 4.0 verified at the host; image origin and contributors' consent to open release not documented
verified: The Zenodo record's metadata gives the licence {"id": "cc-by-4.0"}; access 'open'; version 01; published 2023-08-26; DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8286529; creators from Mbeya University of Science and Technology, NM-AIST, DevData Analytics, Makerere AI Lab, TARI and SCAAP.
The Zenodo record's description has no statement about licence, consent or restrictions.

The associated article (PMC12020891; the article itself is CC BY) reports 58,709 field images of potato leaves (healthy, early blight, late blight) captured by researchers, farmers and agricultural extension officers with smartphones on farms in Tanzania's Southern Highlands from 22 November 2022 to 8 April 2023, with class labels validated by plant pathologists, and says data was collected with informed consent (tool-reported, paraphrased).
The article's limitations: two diseases only, mostly well-lit images, mainly one variety.
unresolved: Whether every photograph was taken by the project team or by farmers, and whether the farmers' consent covers publication under CC BY 4.0 (the article speaks of consent for data collection)
Commercial-use and redistribution statements beyond the CC BY 4.0 licence itself
The label-validation procedure is described only briefly; no inter-rater agreement is reported

catalog.attribution_text: Laizer, Mduma, Machuve, Lyimo, Babirye, Swai, Siwingwa. Irish Potato Imagery Dataset for Early Detection of Crop Diseases. Zenodo, 2023. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8286529. CC BY 4.0.
catalog.intended_use: Field-image potato blight classification baseline, only once image origin is resolved

evidence.excerpt: "copy and redistribute the material in any medium or format for any purpose, even commercially." "You must give appropriate credit, provide a link to the license, and indicate if changes were made."

entries.outcome: BLOCKED: the host says CC BY 4.0 but the associated article is CC BY-NC; the conflict is unresolved; creator affiliation absent
verified: Mendeley Data shows the licence 'CC BY 4.0' for dataset DOI 10.17632/c2x8rynybg.1 (published 22 July 2025; one contributor, Yongbo Liu; no institution given).
The record says images were 'captured from multiple angles and distances' and manually annotated with LabelImg under plant pathology expert guidance (leaves, fruits and stems; XML files).

The associated Data in Brief article (PMC12553018) states 'This is an open access article under the CC BY-NC license'. It describes a single greenhouse source, class imbalance and RGB-only images, and says the images were taken with an iPhone 14 in a greenhouse; it does not name the photographer.
unresolved: Which licence governs the data: the article's CC BY-NC covers the article text, but the conflict with the dataset label has not been resolved by the creators (a non-commercial licence anywhere on the work is excluded by policy until clarified)
Who took and owns the photographs; the record names one contributor and no institution
Labels were produced by unnamed 'plant pathology specialists'

Common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris) Tanzania dataset (Data in Brief 2026, DOI 10.1016/j.dib.2026.112909): a promising field-image lead (article is CC BY; images taken in farm fields; reviewed by extension officers and plant pathologists), but its Zenodo record was not identified and no dataset licence was read. Not entered.
